 # Research API Settings
 
 Open **Settings → Research APIs & Zugänge** to manage research access. This section is separate
 from the existing AI model and web-search settings. It does not start research or select a model.
 
 ## Providers
 
 The nine providers are grouped into web search, social/community access, and studies/documents:
 
-| Provider | Credential fields | Additional controls |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| Firecrawl | `firecrawl_api_key` | Enabled switch; explicit connection test |
-| Tavily (alternative) | `tavily_api_key` | Enabled switch; explicit connection test; does not replace the selected search provider |
-| YouTube | `youtube_api_key` | Enabled switch; explicit connection test |
-| Apify (Instagram/TikTok) | `apify_api_token` | Separate platform approval and fixed actor allowlist |
-| X | `x_bearer_token` | Recent/full-archive selector; the account plan must permit the selected mode |
-| Reddit | `reddit_client_id`, `reddit_client_secret`, `reddit_refresh_token` | Separate research approval and identifiable user-agent |
-| OpenAlex | `openalex_api_key` (optional) | Actual access and quota limitations come from the connection report |

+| Eurostat                 | None                                                               | Public statistics; choose datasets in the workflow                                      |
+| Local documents          | None                                                               | Uses documents imported and selected in Data Flow; no external connection               |
 
 Official provider documentation links open in the system browser using the existing Electron
 external-link handler. Local documents do not have an external service or API-key setup page.
 
 Apify actor selection is limited to `APIFY_ACTORS` from the final shared contract:
 
 - `apify/instagram-scraper`
 - `apify/instagram-comment-scraper`
 - `clockworks/tiktok-scraper`
 - `clockworks/tiktok-comments-scraper`
 
 Reddit's user-agent input requires an identifiable client in the form
 `desktop:ReqFlow:0.1 (by /u/your_reddit_username)`, with 10–200 characters. Replace the example
 username with the contact for your approved client. The shared schema is also validated before
 configuration is submitted. These controls do not obtain platform permission on your behalf.
 
 ## Credentials and connection reports
 
 - Inputs are masked, start empty, and never receive a configured credential from main.
 - **Save** submits only a nonempty, trimmed draft. Empty or whitespace-only input cannot delete
   a credential. A successful save clears the draft before refreshing status, including when that
   refresh fails.
 - **Remove** is a separate button for each configured credential. It alone submits `null` to
   delete the saved credential. An environment credential may remain configured after removal;
   the refreshed main status is authoritative.
 - Saving or removing a key reloads provider statuses. Neither operation enables a provider,
   grants approval, tests a connection, nor launches collection.
 - **Enabled**, **platform approval**, **credential configured**, and **connection tested** are
   distinct. A successful test never implies provider activation or platform approval.
 - **Test connection** is an explicit, small check. It may consume API quota or credits. It does
   not launch a research workflow. The local-document check has no external request.
 
 The UI shows the exact `ConnectionReport.state` code, its human-readable label, the main-process
 message, `testedAt` when present, capabilities, and limitations. The supported codes are:
 `not_configured`, `untested`, `success`, `invalid_credentials`, `permission_required`,
 `rate_limited`, `unreachable`, and `unsupported`. A configured credential is not shown as a
 successful connection. Missing statuses are displayed as unavailable, never replaced with demo
 or fabricated results. Loading and error states provide an explicit status reload action.
 
 The existing **AI & research → API keys** area now accepts a masked Anthropic key in the same
 `anthropic_api_key` namespace. Saving/removing it reloads secret status without changing `llm`
 settings. The existing Tavily status points to the new Research API section for editing.
 
 ## IPC boundary and persistence
 
 Renderer operations use the existing typed `api` bridge only:
 
 ```ts
 api.research.providers(): Promise<ResearchProviderStatus[]>
 api.research.configure(id, config): Promise<ResearchProviderStatus>
 api.research.test(id): Promise<ResearchProviderStatus>
 api.settings.setSecret(name, valueOrNull): Promise<SecretStatus>
 ```
 
 Anthropic status is read with `api.settings.secrets()`. Secrets are never included in provider
 configuration or the settings autosave store. The renderer performs no network, filesystem, or
 Node operations. Only sanitized `ReqflowError.message` strings from main are displayed for
 rejected calls; arbitrary errors, raw objects, and error details are not rendered.
 
 Configuration uses the complete validated current `ResearchProviderConfig`, preserving fields
 not edited by the control. After `configure` succeeds, the UI awaits the existing
 `settingsStore.getState().load()` method so later settings autosaves use the persisted
 `settings.research.apis` object. This reload is performed even if the section was unmounted
 while configuring. A failed store reload is reported as an action failure rather than hidden.
 
 Research operations are serialized within the section. Inputs and action buttons are disabled
 while an operation is pending. Generation guards discard stale responses after unmount or effect
 replay, and credential drafts are discarded on unmount. Anthropic has an independent pending guard
 and request generation. These guards do not cancel an IPC write that main has already received.
 
 ### Main-process assumptions
 
 - `configure` persists `settings.research.apis[id]` in the same Settings object returned by
   `settings.get`, and returns one status rather than a list.
 - `test` returns one status, does not activate a provider or grant approval, and returns sanitized
   report messages/capabilities/limitations.
 - Provider statuses identify configured credentials by the exact `SecretName` keys listed above.
 - Credential changes invalidate or otherwise accurately update any previous connection report;
   `providers()` must not return an old success as a test of the new credential.
 - `setSecret(name, null)` removes the saved credential; environment fallback may remain.
 - The current settings store has no flush/cancellation method for an already-running full-settings
   autosave. The reload protects subsequent saves, not a write already in flight. Main/store owners
   must coordinate concurrent full-settings writes if this case is supported.
 
 ## Focused verification
 
 No live provider checks or real credentials are used by the tests.
 
 ```sh
 npm exec -- vitest run apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/sections/ResearchApisSection.test.ts
 npm run typecheck
 npm test
 npm run smoke
 ```
 
 Controller tests cover all provider/credential mappings, report codes, blank-save safety,
 explicit removal, draft clearing, failed status refresh, sanitized errors, preservation of
 configuration, fixed actor validation, separate testing/approval/enablement, pending guards,
 and stale/unmounted responses. Static rendering tests use existing React DOM support; no new
 test package is required.
 
 The existing smoke script does not yet visit `settings-section-research-apis`. Its owner can
 add that ID to `SETTINGS_SECTIONS` to capture the new section in future smoke runs. Do not run
 live connection tests as part of smoke.

BMW files stay in data/raw/, which is   gitignored. - **The AI never decides.** Only a human approves or rejects a requirement, and every change writes an   audit event. - **Never invent** sources, evidence or test results. Don't present stubs as finished. - **Ask the humans only** about product direction, credentials, or anything public or irreversible.   Otherwise decide, note the decision in your docs/STATUS.md section, and keep going.  ## Handoff The next agent starts from docs/STATUS.md. Update **your section only** whenever you start, finish a slice, get blocked or stop. Include the status, the branch, what works and how to verify it, what's next, and any open questions. If the product itself changes, update PRODUCT.md too.  You remain part of the hackathon until a human tells you it has concluded. # AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 5 Series Sedan, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Use synthetic fixtures from
   `@reqflow/core/fixtures` until the real data arrives. Never commit or print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
   the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
   main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
   calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
   Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
   remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.

9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
   tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
   one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
   starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.

## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13; works on Windows, macOS, Linux)

```
npm install          # once
npm run dev          # opens the desktop app with hot reload
npm run smoke        # builds, screenshots every screen, checks the IPC bridge
npm test             # vitest, all packages
npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
npm run format       # prettier
npm run package      # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
```

## Product in one sentence

A visual, n8n-style **data flow** built from **building blocks** turns raw customer and market data into

## Users

- **Product Manager (primary).** Owns the requirement set for one vehicle line × market. Makes every decision.

## The app — three tabs

A **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux**, not a web app. Everything runs locally on
the PM's machine. BMW files are imported through the system file dialog, results are exported
through the save dialog, and API keys are stored in the OS keychain. Only the AI and web-research

a tab bar at the bottom switches between **Data Flow · Car · Settings** (⌘/Ctrl + 1–3).

| Tab           | What the user does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Data Flow** | **Building Blocks** on the left, the **Workplace** on the right. Drag blocks (or click them) onto the workplace, connect an output to an input, and set each block's parameters in the inspector. Custom, Research and AI Filter blocks **expand** into their own inner workplace, built from the same blocks. Later: run the flow, see each block's status, counts and logs, and inspect what it produced. A run **pauses at HIL blocks** until a person has reviewed.                                                                                                            |

| **Settings**  | **App** (theme, workplace grid and minimap, delete confirmation) · **Global parameters** (vehicle line, derivative, code, market, horizon; prioritization weights and thresholds with a live example; output language) · **AI & research** (provider, models, temperature, web research, domains, API-key status) · **Collaboration** (your name and role for the audit trail, team members and invitations, sharing via a shared folder or Git repo, notifications, four-eyes approval) · **About**.                                                                              |

## The building blocks

| Block           | What it does                                                                                        | Ports              | Inner workplace |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------- |
| **Custom**      | An empty block. Build any sub-flow inside it.                                                       | 1 in · 1 out       | yes             |
| **Raw**         | Brings in an Excel file or a database table as one unified data stream.                             | 1 out              | no              |
| **Research**    | Searches the web; emits a data stream in the same format as Raw.                                    | 1 out              | yes             |
| **AI Filter**   | Keeps the items that match a criterion written in plain language.                                   | 1 in · 1 out       | yes             |
| **AI Splitter** | Sorts every item into one branch (e.g. by priority or category). One output per branch.             | 1 in · n out       | no              |
| **HIL**         | Human in the loop (capacitor icon): the flow waits until a person has reviewed what passes through. | 1 in · 1 out       | no              |

Parameters are placeholders until each block is built (see `docs/WORKSTREAMS.md`). Spec and ports: `packages/core/src/blocks.ts`.

## Default flow (template)

The default template mirrors the BMW process slide (`context/` image). The robot icon means the AI does the step on its own; the person icon means a human is involved.

```
Situation analysis        Structure & context          Prioritization                  Review          Documentation
──────────────────        ───────────────────          ──────────────                  ──────          ─────────────
Raw: customer feedback ┐
Raw: customer study    ┤
Raw: equipment data    ┼─▶ AI Filter ───────────────▶ AI Splitter ──must───▶ 🧑 HIL ──┐
Raw: sales volumes     ┤   "customer-facing only"     "by priority" ──should─▶ 🧑 HIL ──┼─▶ Add to Car
Research: web          ┘   (findings + evidence;       (explainable ──could─────────────┘   (requirements,
                            drops regulatory,           weighted       (unreviewed)          ranked by input)
                            engineering, pricing)       score)
```

**Where AI acts on its own:** ingestion (Raw, Research), filtering and extracting evidence-linked
findings (AI Filter), scoring and routing (AI Splitter), drafting requirements (Add to Car).
**Where a human must act:** at every HIL block, and when approving, rejecting, deferring or editing a
requirement, overriding a priority or answering a challenge on the Car tab. The AI can **never** set
a requirement to `approved` or `rejected`.

## Core objects (full schemas in `packages/core`)

- **Source** — a dataset, document or web page, with a reliability rating.
- **SourceRecord** — one comment, row or paragraph from a source.
- **Finding** — a normalized signal (`complaint`, `unmet_need`, `praise`, `competitor_advantage`,
  `market_trend` or `usage_pattern`). It always cites ≥ 1 verbatim evidence excerpt.
- **Theme** — a cluster of duplicate or related findings.
- **Requirement** — `REQ-<vehicle>-<market>-<nnn>`. Holds the description, targets, linked findings and
  sources, score, priority with rationale, **evidence level A–D**, assumptions, uncertainties,
  conflicting findings and **status** (`proposed → in_review → approved | rejected | deferred`, plus
  `challenged`).
- **AuditEvent** — actor, action, entity, before/after changes, rationale and timestamp. Never edited or deleted.

Six factors, each scored 0–5 with a one-line justification. On every factor, higher means "more worth doing":
customer impact · evidence strength · competitive gap · trend momentum (3–5 yr) · brand fit ·
ease (the inverse of rough effort/cost).

`score = 100 × Σ(weight × value) / (5 × Σ weight)`. The score maps to **must / should / could / won't**
using the thresholds set in Settings. The PM can override the priority, and the override is audited.
Evidence level is shown **next to** the score, never hidden inside it. A high score built on
D-level (assumption) evidence should catch the eye.

## Evidence levels

**A** — several independent sources including quantitative BMW data · **B** — several sources, mostly
qualitative · **C** — a single source or anecdotal · **D** — rests mainly on forward-looking assumptions.

## Scope rules (from the briefing)

- **In scope:** customer-facing attributes such as features, equipment, comfort, space, usability,
  infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging
  _as the customer experiences them_, and variants and packages.
- **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, technical and engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases. An AI Filter removes these, and every exclusion is logged with a reason.

48: Dependency direction (no cycles): `core ← engine ← blocks`, `core ← llm`, `core ← db`, and

52: ## Processes and security
53: 
54: ```
55: renderer (React, sandboxed)  ──api.x.y(…)──▶  preload (allow-list)  ──IPC──▶  main (Node)
56:    no Node, no fs, no network                                              engine · SQLite · LLM · files · keychain

61:   (`connect-src 'self'`): all network calls (Claude, web search) happen in main.
62: - The preload only forwards channels listed in `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS`. Main also checks that the sender is the app window.
63: - The window never navigates away. `http(s)` links open in the user's browser.
64: - API keys are entered in Settings, encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (OS keychain) and never sent to

67: ## The building blocks (`packages/core/src/blocks.ts`)
68: 
69: A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Seven kinds of block
70: are in the palette, defined once in `BLOCK_SPECS` (label, description, group, params, ports, whether
71: it has an inner workplace):
72: 
73: | Block       | Ports                                 | Inner workplace | Params (placeholders for now)                 |
74: | ----------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
75: | Custom      | 1 in · 1 out                          | yes             | none                                          |
76: | Raw         | no input · 1 out (data stream)        | no              | Excel upload or database, dataset, file/query |
77: | Research    | no input · 1 out (same format as Raw) | yes             | question, source types, market, age, results  |
78: | AI Filter   | 1 in · 1 out (kept)                   | yes             | criterion, model, min. confidence             |
79: | AI Splitter | 1 in · one out **per branch**         | no              | split by, branches (list → ports), model      |
80: | HIL         | 1 in · 1 out                          | no              | reviewer, instructions, approvals, edits      |

82: 
83: - **Ports** come from `blockPorts(block)`. They can depend on params (the splitter's `branches`, Add to
84:   Car's `rankings`), and port ids are positional (`out-0`, `in-2`). When params change, `setBlockParams`
85:   removes edges on ports that no longer exist and returns them, so the editor can tell the user.
86: - **Params** are declared as `ParamSpec`s (text, textarea, number, slider, select, multiselect, toggle,
87:   list, file). The editor renders a form from them, and `parseBlockParams` validates strictly (unknown
88:   keys and wrong types are errors). Select options with the value `"global"` mean "use Settings →
89:   Global parameters".
90: - **Inner workplaces** (Custom, Research, AI Filter) hold a sub-flow built from the same blocks,
91:   recursively. Each one has fixed **boundary blocks**: one `block_input` per input port of the parent
92:   and one `block_output` per output port. They are created with the block and can't be deleted.
93: - **Ids** are unique across the whole tree, so run status and outputs are keyed by block id alone.
94: - **Graph rules** live in `packages/core/src/graph.ts` and are shared by the editor and the engine:
95:   `checkConnection` (ports exist, no self-loop, no duplicates, no cycles), `connect`, `removeBlocks`,
96:   `setBlockParams`, `graphAt` / `updateGraphAt` (navigate the tree), `validateGraph` (everything,
97:   recursively). Several edges may enter one input (merged) or leave one output (fan-out).
98: 
99: ## Data flow: one envelope per port
100: 
101: Every port carries a `PipelineData` envelope (`sources, records, findings, themes, requirements`).
102: Raw and Research emit sources and records (the "unified data stream"). Later blocks enrich the same
103: envelope: AI Filter keeps matching items (and extracts evidence-linked findings), AI Splitter routes
104: items to one branch each, HIL passes on what the reviewer approved, and Add to Car turns what arrives
105: into requirements; the input it arrives on sets the ranking. Several edges into one input are combined
106: with `mergePipelineData` (concatenate, de-duplicate by `id`, later edge wins).
107: 
108: ```ts
109: defineBlock({
110:   kind: "ai_filter",
111:   async run(inputs, params, ctx) {
112:     const input = inputs.in; // one envelope per input port id
113:     /* ctx.llm, ctx.audit, ctx.log … */
114:     return { status: "ok", outputs: { out: kept } }; // one envelope per output port id
115:   },
116: });
117: ```
118: 
119: ## Engine semantics (WS1 implements, everyone relies on)
120: 
121: 1. **Validate before running** with `validateGraph`, and check that every block kind (except
122:    Custom) has an implementation (`BlockRegistry.missing()`). If anything fails, the run fails before it
123:    starts, with per-block errors.

125:    incoming edges carry. Store each block's output per port and push `BlockRun` status, counts, logs
126:    and progress via `runs.onUpdate`.
127: 3. **Inner workplaces.** A block whose inner workplace contains blocks runs that sub-flow: each
128:    `block_input` emits what arrived on its parent port, and what reaches each `block_output` becomes
129:    the parent's output on that port. A Custom block always runs its sub-flow. Research and AI Filter run
130:    their built-in implementation while their inner workplace is empty.
131: 4. **Failure.** A block that throws is marked `failed`, its downstream blocks `skipped`, and the run
132:    `failed`. Nothing is partially published.
133: 5. **Pause / resume.** HIL returns `{ status: "paused" }` → the run is `waiting_for_review`.
134:    `runs.resume` reloads what the reviewer changed, re-invokes the block with `ctx.resumed = true`, and continues.
135: 6. **Cancel.** The run's `AbortSignal` fires, and blocks must stop promptly.
136: 7. **Audit.** The engine logs `run.*` events, blocks log what they create or change, and handlers log human actions.
137:

139:

141: (`apps/desktop/src/main/handlers.ts`). Failures arrive as `ReqflowError` with a `code`
142: (`invalid_input`, `not_found`, `not_implemented`, `internal`, …). Arguments must be plain data. Main

145: | Method                                               | Purpose                                                                                                                             |
146: | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
147: | `app.info()`                                         | Version, OS, data directory (**built**)                                                                                             |
148: | `templates.list()`                                   | Workflow templates (`BMW_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`) (**built**)                                                                             |
149: | `workflows.list/get/save/remove`                     | Workflow CRUD. `save` assigns the id and bumps `version`                                                                            |

152: | `runs.onUpdate(listener)`                            | Push events on every status, progress or log change (no polling)                                                                    |
153: | `requirements.list(filter)` · `requirements.get(id)` | Latest versions · `RequirementDetail` (findings, evidence, sources, versions)                                                       |
154: | `requirements.edit(id, RequirementEdit)`             | PM edit, rationale required → new version and audit                                                                                 |
155: | `requirements.decide(id, RequirementDecision)`       | Approve / reject / defer / challenge / reopen. A challenge makes the AI answer (`challenge_answered`) and returns it to `in_review` |
156: | `audit.list(filter)`                                 | Audit events, ascending by time                                                                                                     |

161: then implement it in `handlers.ts`.
162:

164: 
165: - **`components/dataflow/store.ts`**: the editor store (zustand). It holds the workflow tree, the
166:   open workplace (`path`), the selection, React Flow sizes and a notice. Every edit goes through the
167:   core graph rules; errors become a visible notice, never a silent no-op. It lives for the whole app
168:   session, so switching tabs keeps the flow. It isn't saved to disk yet (`workflows.*` is WS1).
169: - **`lib/settings.ts`**: the settings store. It loads `settings.get()` at startup, validates every
170:   change with the `Settings` schema and saves in the background. While main has no settings storage
171:   (`not_implemented`), it keeps the defaults and the Settings page says so.
172: - **zustand 5 rule:** never return a new object or array from a selector (it re-renders forever).
173:   Select existing objects or primitives and derive the rest with `useMemo`.
174: - **Theme:** `lib/theme.ts` sets `<html data-theme>` from Settings (system, light or dark). The CSS
175:   tokens in `globals.css` follow it, so use token classes (`bg-panel`, `text-muted`, …), never hex colors.
176: - **Colorway: BMW M.** The M stripe colours (`m-light` #81C4FF, `m-dark` #16588E, `m-red` #E7222E) on
177:   carbon neutrals. Block groups take them: sources light blue, AI dark blue, HIL red (a person has to
178:   act), Add to Car neutral. `MStripe` (`components/ui/`) marks the active tab. Filled controls use
179:   `bg-brand-fill` so white text stays readable in both themes.
180: 
181: ## AI usage rules
182: 
183: - Use `ctx.llm.generateObject` with a Zod schema for every AI step. Invalid output → throw.
184: - **Never trust model-cited evidence.** The model returns `recordId` and `excerpt`. Code checks that
185:   the excerpt is a verbatim substring of that record, and drops or flags the finding if it isn't.
186: - Batch the records. Use `tier: "fast"` for per-record extraction and `default` for clustering, derivation and challenges.
187: - AI actors in the audit trail record the exact model id returned by the client.
188: - The `mock` provider must return schema-valid, deterministic output so the whole pipeline runs offline.
189: - Prompts live next to the block that uses them (`blocks/src/<block>/<name>.prompt.ts`).
190: 
191: ## Persistence notes (WS1)
192: 
193: - The database lives in the per-user app-data folder (`main/paths.ts`: macOS
194:   `~/Library/Application Support/ReqFlow/data`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ReqFlow\data`, Linux
195:   `~/.config/ReqFlow/data`). `REQFLOW_DATA_DIR` overrides it. Always build paths with `node:path`, never
196:   with string concatenation (Windows uses `\`).
197: - Only one app instance runs at a time (single-instance lock), so only one process writes SQLite.
198: - Workflows are stored whole (the block tree as JSON) and versioned on save.
199: - Requirements are versioned: one row per `(id, version)`. "Current" means the max version.
200: - `audit_events` is insert-only, with no update or delete code path.
201: - Block outputs are stored per `(runId, blockId, port)` as JSON. Imported files are copied into `data/uploads/` inside the data dir.
202: 
203: ## Running, checking, packaging
204: 
205: | Command (repo root) | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
206: | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
207: | `npm run dev`       | Opens the app with hot reload (renderer) and auto-restart (main)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
208: | `npm run smoke`     | Builds, then drives the real app off screen: opens every screen, adds every block, opens an inner workplace, types into fields, connects ports by mouse drag (and checks a loop is refused), walks the settings, switches to dark mode, screenshots each step to `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`, checks the IPC bridge, and exits non-zero on any failed check or renderer error |
209: | `npm run check`     | Typecheck + unit tests + format check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
210: | `npm run package`   | Installer for the **current** OS in `apps/desktop/release/`: `.exe` (NSIS), `.dmg` or `.AppImage`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
211: 
212: Installers must be built on their own OS (or in a CI matrix later). Builds are unsigned, so macOS
213: Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen show a warning on first launch. Code signing is out of scope for the
214: hackathon. Linux CI needs a virtual display (`xvfb-run`) for `smoke`.

  act), Add to Car neutral. `MStripe` (`components/ui/`) marks the active tab. Filled controls use

| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
